en: In a different version of the *Amitābha Sūtra*, following the phrase "single-mindedness without distraction," there are twenty-one characters stating: "By exclusively holding the Name, because of this recitation of the Name, all transgressions are extinguished;
this is the causal condition of many roots of goodness and merit."
This is the text of the *Śālistamba-sūtra* from the stone carving at Xiangyang. Yuanzhao and Jidu both considered it a lost passage.

Zuhong, however, stated: "Regarding the words of previous commentators that have been mixed into the main text—considering that the Sanskrit original was repetitive and emphatic, while the translators occasionally employed omissions—did the translators omit them, or did they [not]?"
[This] has been omitted. Whether it was subsequently lost or not, all remains unknown. The *Longshu Jingtuwén* states:
"The Stone Sutras of Xiangyang were transcribed by Chen Rénléng of the Sui dynasty; their calligraphy is elegant and graceful, and many people admire and play with them.
During the Taireki era, Taira Munemori dispatched an envoy to the Song to seek the Tripitaka and the Stone Sutras. In the autumn of the ninth year of the Kenju era..."
An envoy from the Song dynasty brought the Stone Classics (Shijing) aboard ship; the vessel ran aground at Zuiō in Chikuzen, and rubbings of the texts were transmitted to the world.
Within these texts, "Jile" (極樂) is written as "Zuole" (作為), and "zhongsheng guo" (眾生國) is written as "zotu" (作土). In all cases, "sheng" (生) is written as "sheng" (生);
thus, "ziran sheng" (自然生) is written as "ziran jie sheng" (自然皆生). However, other editions also contain the same readings; it is only these twenty-one characters that differ.
This is found exclusively in the Stone Classics of Xiangyang.
Recorded by Akamatsu Renjō on the first day of the tenth month in the first year of Taishō.
